author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Oracle Executive Chairman Larry Ellison has canceled a trading plan that would have allowed him to sell up to 50 million Oracle shares, the company said Saturday. The plan had been announced only a day earlier. Oracle said no shares were sold under it and Ellison currently has no intention to sell his holdings.

The reversal arrives while Oracle is raising substantial capital to expand cloud infrastructure for artificial-intelligence demand. The company plans to raise between $45 billion and $50 billion during calendar 2026 through debt and equity financing. It is targeting $40 billion during the current fiscal year, including a $20 billion stock sale completed in the first quarter.

Oracle is balancing that investment push against restructuring costs and investor sensitivity to the pace and financing of AI expansion. The company reported $700 million in restructuring expenses, including job cuts. Its shares had briefly gained after a $26 billion increase in revenue backlog but closed Friday about 2% lower, according to Reuters. Those figures describe completed market moves, not live pricing. Canceling Ellison’s planned sale removes one potential source of near-term share supply while Oracle continues its much larger corporate financing program.
dek: Oracle said no shares were sold and its executive chairman currently has no intention to reduce his holdings.
headline: Larry Ellison cancels plan to sell 50 million Oracle shares
